excerpt: Three costs almost every company underestimates when building an in-house field team: hiring, training, and turnover.
meta_description: The three hidden costs — hiring, training, and turnover — that make DIY field marketing teams more expensive than they appear.
author: SIT™ Editorial
seo_title: Hidden Costs of In-House Field Teams — SIT™
title: Hiring, Training, Turnover — The Hidden Costs of DIY Outreach
content:
###  **Cost One — Hiring** 

Posting a job, screening applicants, and interviewing candidates all take real hours — hours a business owner or manager could otherwise spend running the business or serving existing customers. 

###  **Cost Two — Training** 

Field work is not intuitive. Someone has to teach a new hire how to represent the brand, how to have a conversation with a stranger at their door, how to handle rejection professionally. That training investment happens whether or not the person stays. 

###  **Cost Three — Turnover** 

Field roles see some of the highest turnover rates of any job category. Every person who leaves after a few weeks takes the training investment with them, and the cycle starts over. 

### **Why This Adds Up Differently Than Expected** 

None of these costs show up as a single line item — they are spread out and easy to underestimate until a company tallies a full season and realizes how much went into a team that never became consistent. 

###  **Worth Comparing** 

A structured field marketing pilot is often the fastest way to see what consistent, professional outreach actually costs — without the hiring and training investment upfront.
